cases.description: A complete single-stream record should pass every audit and produce all three grounded T661 lines.
text:
## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended December 31, 2025.

## Technical objective
During the claimed year, the team sought a controller that held spindle vibration below 2 mm/s while the mounted load changed during operation.

## Starting knowledge
At the start of the project, the fixed-gain controller reached 8 mm/s when load inertia changed. Published gain-tuning methods assumed a constant load and could not predict the changing-load response of this spindle.

## Technological uncertainty
It was unknown whether a load-state observer could preserve closed-loop stability while adapting controller bandwidth as the load changed.

## Hypothesis and work
The team hypothesized that scheduling observer bandwidth from estimated load inertia would reduce vibration without destabilizing the loop. During 2025, claimant engineers tested four bandwidth schedules under three changing-load profiles while recording vibration and phase margin.

## Results and conclusion
The fastest schedule became unstable and was rejected. The selected schedule reached 1.8 mm/s across all three profiles. The team concluded that observer bandwidth had to decrease as estimated load inertia increased.

## Advancement
The work established the relationship between estimated load inertia, observer bandwidth, and closed-loop stability for this changing-load spindle architecture.

## Records
Dated test matrices, controller versions, vibration traces, phase-margin calculations, and decision notes record the hypothesis, tests, results, and conclusion.

## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended June 30, 2025.

## Objective and starting point
During the claimed year, the team needed an image-registration method that tolerated non-rigid specimen motion. The existing rigid transform left visible edge misalignment, and published rigid registration methods did not address local deformation in these image sequences.

## Uncertainty
The team did not know whether a spatially constrained deformation model could correct local motion without distorting stable regions.

## Work described by the client
The team believed regional constraints might preserve stable areas and says three model variants were tested during 2025. The client has not provided the observed output of any variant, the conclusion reached, the knowledge gained, or the records supporting the tests.

## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended December 31, 2025.

## Current problem
During 2025, the existing controller produced 8 mm/s vibration, and standard fixed-gain tuning could not maintain stability as load changed. It remained unknown whether an adaptive observer could meet the 2 mm/s target.

## Proposed work
In 2026 the team will test five observer designs and compare vibration, phase margin, and response time. The expected result is 1.8 mm/s. Test logs will be created after the experiments. No prototype, experiment, simulation, measurement, or analysis was completed during 2025.

## Expected learning
The planned work should establish how observer bandwidth affects stability.

cases.description: Routine vendor configuration with an achieved business result must not be reframed as technological uncertainty or advancement.

## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended March 31, 2025.

## Project
The company wanted weekly management dashboards and faster report preparation. Staff followed the cloud vendor documentation to enable the standard analytics module, selected existing dashboard templates, configured documented data connectors, and scheduled weekly exports.

## Outcome
The vendor-supported configuration worked as documented. Report preparation fell from two days to two hours. No hypothesis, experiment, technological uncertainty, custom algorithm, or advancement in the underlying software was involved. Configuration tickets and user-training notes record the implementation.

cases.description: Directly conflicting accounts of who performed the experiments must block claimant drafting and expose the conflict.

## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended September 30, 2025.

## Technical account
The objective was to keep coating variation below 3%. The standard spray path produced 12% variation, and supplier settings could not predict deposition over the curved surface. It was unknown whether synchronized nozzle acceleration could maintain uniform deposition.

## Investigation account A
The project manager states that claimant engineers hypothesized that synchronized acceleration would prevent edge pooling. The project manager states that claimant engineers tested four paths during 2025, observed 2.6% variation on the fourth path, concluded that acceleration timing controlled edge pooling, and established the relationship between path curvature and required acceleration.

## Investigation account B
A signed vendor statement says the vendor independently designed and performed all four experiments using its own facility and staff. It says the claimant did not direct or perform the experiments and only installed the vendor's final package. Both accounts refer to the same four tests and cannot both be correct.

## Records
Path files, measurement sheets, photographs, and the two conflicting signed statements are available.

cases.description: Two independently supported uncertainties should produce two audited SIS chains and an enforced split or hybrid report.
text:
## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended December 31, 2025.

## TU-A objective and uncertainty
During 2025 the optical subsystem had to resolve 90 nm features at a 4 mm working distance. The prior pole-piece resolved only 180 nm. Published symmetric pole-piece equations assumed a longer column and could not predict aberration in the shortened geometry. It was unknown whether an asymmetric pole-piece could recover resolution without losing focus repeatability.

## TU-A systematic investigation
The team hypothesized that an asymmetric return path would reduce spherical aberration. Claimant engineers simulated five geometries and built three prototypes during 2025. Geometry A resolved 130 nm but lost focus after sample-height changes. Geometry B saturated the lens current. Geometry C repeatedly resolved 88 nm and retained focus. The team concluded that return-path asymmetry, rather than a smaller gap alone, controlled aberration in the shortened column. The work established the relationship between return-path asymmetry, lens saturation, and achievable resolution. Dated simulation files, CAD revisions, images, focus logs, and review notes record this sequence.

## TU-B objective and uncertainty
During 2025 the detector subsystem had to preserve signal-to-noise ratio above 12 at low beam current without disturbing the beam. The existing side detector reached an SNR of 6. Supplier placement guidance assumed a conventional column and could not predict field interaction near the compact pole-piece. It was unknown whether an annular detector and revised shielding could improve collection without deflecting the beam.

## TU-B systematic investigation
The team hypothesized that segmented annular collection with a grounded inner shield would reduce field distortion. Claimant engineers tested three detector distances, four bias settings, and two shield geometries during 2025. The closest unshielded setting reached SNR 15 but displaced the beam and was rejected. The grounded inner shield reached SNR 13 without measurable displacement. The team concluded that the shield boundary, not bias alone, controlled the trade-off. The work established how detector distance, bias, and the grounded shield interacted in the compact field geometry. Dated detector drawings, bias logs, SNR traces, beam-position images, and decision notes record this sequence.

cases.description: A well-documented investigation may support drafting even when every tested approach failed to meet the objective.
text:
## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended December 31, 2025.

## Objective and starting knowledge
During 2025 the claimant sought a membrane stack that resisted solvent swelling while preserving ion transport. The prior fluoropolymer stack delaminated after repeated solvent exposure. Published lamination guidance addressed aqueous service and could not predict bond behaviour in the mixed-solvent cycle.

## Technological uncertainty
It was unknown whether a graded interlayer could maintain adhesion without blocking ion transport during the mixed-solvent cycle.

## Hypothesis and work
The team hypothesized that a graded porosity interlayer would spread solvent-induced strain while retaining connected ion pathways. Claimant scientists fabricated four interlayer gradients during 2025 and exposed each stack to repeated mixed-solvent cycles while recording delamination and transport behaviour.

## Results and conclusion
All four gradients failed. Two dense gradients prevented delamination but blocked ion transport; two open gradients transported ions but delaminated. The team concluded that porosity alone could not decouple strain transfer from transport in this material pair and abandoned that interlayer architecture.

## Attempted advancement
The investigation established a boundary condition: within the tested material pair, the porosity needed for connected ion transport also transmitted enough solvent-induced strain to defeat the bond. This unsuccessful result narrowed the feasible design space beyond the starting knowledge.

## Records
Dated fabrication sheets, cycle logs, microscopy images, transport traces, failed-sample photographs, and the abandonment decision record the investigation.

cases.description: A complete mathematical and simulation investigation must not be blocked merely because no physical prototype was built.
text:
## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended October 31, 2025.

## Objective and baseline
During the claimed year the claimant needed to predict recirculation in a compact heat exchanger with pulsed inlet flow. The existing steady-flow correlation underpredicted the observed recirculation region. Published correlations assumed steady fully developed flow and did not resolve the pulsed geometry.

## Technological uncertainty
It was unknown whether a phase-resolved reduced-order model could preserve the vortex transition while remaining computationally usable for design iterations.

## Hypothesis and analysis
The team hypothesized that phase-conditioned basis functions would preserve the transition lost by a time-averaged basis. During 2025 claimant engineers derived both formulations and ran transient simulations across six pulse profiles, comparing vortex onset, recirculation direction, and solution stability. No physical prototype was required for this analytical investigation.

## Results and conclusion
The time-averaged basis reversed the predicted recirculation direction in the accelerating phase. The phase-conditioned basis preserved the observed transition across the six profiles but became unstable when the phase bins were made too narrow. The team concluded that phase conditioning was necessary and that a minimum bin width governed stability.

## Advancement and records
The work established how phase-bin width controlled the trade-off between vortex-transition fidelity and reduced-order stability in this pulsed geometry. Dated derivations, solver versions, run manifests, field plots, comparison tables, and review notes record the sequence.

text:
## Project account
The team sought a scheduler that maintained queue fairness when workloads changed abruptly. The existing weighted scheduler starved short jobs, and published tuning guidance assumed stationary arrival rates. It was unknown whether an age-sensitive weight could preserve fairness without reducing throughput.

## Investigation
The team hypothesized that a capped age term would prevent starvation. Engineers simulated four caps under burst and recovery workloads. A low cap still starved short jobs, while the selected cap restored fairness without the throughput collapse seen at the highest cap. The team concluded that the cap had to track the recovery interval.

## Advancement and records
The work established the relationship between recovery interval, age cap, and starvation behaviour. Test manifests, scheduler commits, traces, and decision notes are available. The client material does not identify the company's claimed tax year or state when this work occurred.

## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended December 31, 2025.

## Technical context
The objective was to control thermal drift in a compact optical mount. The prior static offset left focus changes after rapid temperature cycling, and standard static compensation could not predict the history-dependent response. It was unknown whether a state-dependent compensation model could preserve focus after cycling.

## Engineering narrative
The engineering summary says claimant engineers hypothesized that two thermal-history states were sufficient, tested five state-transition models during 2025, observed that the fifth reduced drift, and concluded that the cooling-rate state controlled the residual response.

## Dated record conflict
The signed experiment ledger dates all five model runs and the technical conclusion to November 2024. The 2025 change log records only installation of the completed model and operator training. The engineering summary and signed ledger refer to the same five runs, so both chronologies cannot be correct.

## Records
The engineering summary, signed experiment ledger, model files, 2025 deployment log, and operator-training record are available.

cases.description: One uncertainty addressed by two complete investigation paths should remain one TU and use separate SIS sections.
text:
## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended December 31, 2025.

## Objective and uncertainty
During 2025 the claimant needed a robotic gripper that retained irregular wet parts without surface damage. The prior fixed-pressure jaws either slipped or marked the parts. Published rigid-contact calculations assumed known dry friction and could not predict the changing wet contact. It was unknown whether grip force could be controlled from indirect contact signals under those conditions.

## SIS-A acoustic path
The team first hypothesized that high-frequency acoustic energy would identify incipient slip before gross motion. Claimant engineers tested three sensor positions and four frequency bands during 2025. Motor noise masked two bands, while the highest band detected slip only after visible movement. The team concluded that acoustic sensing could not provide sufficiently early control input in the existing actuator assembly. Acoustic traces, videos, sensor layouts, and the rejection note record SIS-A.

## SIS-B compliance path
The team then hypothesized that the rate of change in jaw compliance would identify fluid displacement before slip. Claimant engineers tested three compliant pad geometries across dry, misted, and saturated parts during 2025. One pad produced a repeatable compliance change before motion without leaving marks; the softer pad delayed the signal and was rejected. The team concluded that a bounded pad stiffness was necessary for an early control signal. Force traces, pad revisions, videos, and the selection note record SIS-B.

## Advancement
Together the investigations established that acoustic energy was too actuator-dependent for early detection and that pre-slip fluid displacement could instead be inferred from compliance change within a bounded pad-stiffness range.

cases.description: Evidence fragments from two streams must not be combined into a false complete investigation chain.

## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended December 31, 2025.

## TU-A thermal control
During 2025 the thermal stream sought stable chamber temperature after door openings. The prior proportional controller overshot, and standard fixed-gain tuning could not predict the changing air mass. It was unknown whether a state estimator could stabilize recovery. The team hypothesized that a two-state estimator would separate wall and air response and tested three gain sets. The client supplied no observed results, technical conclusion, advancement, or dated records for this stream.

## TU-B optical correction
During 2025 the optical stream sought focus stability during stage acceleration. The prior static correction left direction-dependent blur, and standard static calibration did not account for acceleration history. It was unknown whether an acceleration-state correction could remove the blur. The team tested two correction tables and observed that the second removed the direction-dependent blur. The team concluded that acceleration sign had to be represented explicitly. However, the source does not state the hypothesis that led to those tables, the knowledge advanced beyond that conclusion, or which dated records support this stream.

## Separation note
The thermal and optical work concerned different subsystems, variables, tests, and outcomes. A result or conclusion from one stream does not answer a missing link in the other.

cases.description: A complete investigation with precise qualitative observations should not require an invented numerical measurement.
text:
## Reporting period
The claimed tax year ended August 31, 2025.

## Objective and baseline
During 2025 the claimant sought a ceramic firing profile that prevented edge cracking in a layered component while retaining a continuous conductive path. The prior uniform ramp produced edge cracks. Published single-material firing guidance did not predict stress evolution across the layered interface.

## Technological uncertainty
It was unknown whether staging the binder-removal interval could release edge stress without interrupting conductive-particle contact.

## Hypothesis and work
The team hypothesized that a staged hold before densification would let the outer layer relax before the conductive layer locked in. Claimant engineers fired specimens using a uniform ramp, an early staged hold, and a late staged hold during 2025, then examined crack location, interface shape, and continuity under the same inspection method.

## Observations and conclusion
The uniform ramp repeatedly produced cracks beginning at the outer edge. The late hold moved the cracks into the interface. The early hold produced intact edges and a visibly continuous conductive path across every inspected section. The team concluded that stress had to be released before conductive-layer lock-in rather than during densification.

## Advancement and records
The work established the sequence relationship between binder-removal timing, interface stress relocation, and conductive-path continuity in the layered component. Dated kiln programs, specimen maps, section images, inspection notes, and the profile-selection record support the investigation.
